create.name: Catherine Ingram
create.bio:
Catherine Ingram is an American-born dharma teacher who now lives in Victoria, Australia, and has gathered students in North America, Europe and Australia for more than three decades. In 1976 she was among the group that set up the Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts, and she spent the following years as a journalist writing on consciousness and activism for magazines including Yoga Journal and East West Journal. She has also worked for Tibetan, Burmese and animal welfare causes, and helped start the Unrepresented Nations and Peoples Organization in The Hague.

Since the early 1990s her main form of teaching has been Dharma Dialogues: open meetings where a short period of silence leads into frank conversation about attention, love, loss, work and the ordinary difficulties of a life, alongside silent retreats. These days the dialogues mostly happen on Zoom, and recordings appear on her podcast, In the Deep, and her YouTube channel. She also offers private conversations by phone. Her books are Passionate Presence, on seven qualities of awakened awareness; In the Footsteps of Gandhi, interviews with spiritual and social activists; and a novel, A Crack in Everything.

books.title: Passionate Presence: Seven Qualities of Awakened Awareness
books.author: Catherine Ingram
books.description: Catherine's best-known book, first published in 2003, looks at seven qualities that show up when attention rests in the present, among them tenderness, delight and silence. Stories from her retreats and dialogues run through each chapter.

books.title: In the Footsteps of Gandhi: Conversations with Spiritual Social Activists
books.author: Catherine Ingram
books.description: Interviews from Catherine's years as a journalist with people who joined inner practice to work for peace and justice, including the Dalai Lama, Thich Nhat Hanh and Desmond Tutu. Each conversation asks how nonviolence works in practice.

courses.title: Private sessions with Catherine
courses.description: One-to-one conversations with Catherine by telephone, booked and paid for by email; she makes the call. Choose half an hour or a full hour.

free_resources.title: Catherine Ingram on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Recorded talks and short reflections from Catherine on themes such as letting go, solitude and the end of seeking, free to hear in the app or on the web.

free_resources.title: In the Deep with Catherine Ingram (podcast)
free_resources.description: Catherine's free podcast of recent Dharma Dialogues on Zoom and remastered recordings from earlier decades. New episodes appear every few weeks, on topics from attention and desire to grief and authenticity.

free_resources.title: Life Advice columns
free_resources.description: An archive of the question-and-answer column Catherine wrote for four years for a Pacific Northwest magazine, answering readers' letters about family, relationships and living with intention.

sprint.tier_evidence: Insight Timer 4.4k (profile via WebFetch, 1 Nov 2026); YouTube 1.24k (@DharmaDialogues header row, 1 Nov 2026); no Instagram, Facebook or X linked from her site (an Instagram @catherineingram with 104 followers exists but is not linked, so not counted) → ~5.6k total → local_hero
flags: Possible editorial-stature case: her site says she co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (an existing hub) in 1976 and she wrote Passionate Presence; left at local_hero for the owner to decide.

Her site's 'Facing Extinction' page says she was 'propagandized into climate hysteria' and was wrong about climate data, and names AI and transhumanism as the real threat; not linked from the plan, but a reviewer may want a political check, as with Steven Webb and Rachel Ricketts.
Her YouTube channel picture looks as if it may be AI-generated or heavily edited, so it was not used; both photos are from her own site.

Insight Timer gives her base as Melbourne; her podcast says recordings come from Victoria, Australia. No in-person programme is listed (schedule page says only 'watch this space'), so availability is worldwide.
Email is an AOL address named for her Dharma Dialogues; it is the one published on her contact and private sessions pages.
Only one offering (phone sessions); the page relies on videos, books and free resources.
left_out: A Crack in Everything (novel, ASIN 0978919300): amazon.com /dp/ returned 500 three times, not verified.
Videos 'Addicted to Craving', 'Brokenhearted', 'No Matter What You've Suffered' and podcast 'Rumination and Depression': condition or borderline framing.
Videos 'Living with Fear' and 'A Non-Anxious Presence' (2009–10 webcast clips with others): fear/anxiety titles and short clips.
Her 2021 TED talk on the Facing Extinction essay: she has since withdrawn the essay.
Silent retreats and Zoom Dharma Dialogues: no dates or booking pages currently published.
